title: debian-apt-snapshot-prep-and-oci-pruner
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a Debian/Ubuntu apt snapshot indexer for air-gapped bundles and an OCI registry pruning tool to keep offline bundles size-bounded. Terraform module exposes TTL/retention for bundle storage; Helm chart includes apt-overlay sidecar and preflight hooks. Backwards compatible with existing offline bundle format.
description:
Title: Debian APT snapshot indexer + OCI pruner for compact offline bundles

Summary: This PR introduces two coordinated improvements for on-prem/air-gapped Private installer workflows: 1) a delta-based APT snapshot indexer that generates minimal metadata necessary to reproduce apt repositories inside an offline bundle (reduces .deb churn and index size), and 2) an OCI registry pruning controller that enforces TTL/size retention on local registry seeds used for air-gapped installs. The goal is to reduce bundle sizes for customers with stable package sets and provide a configurable retention model for seeded OCI registries so long-lived installations don't accumulate unused layers.

Motivation and context: Over the last two quarters we've seen multiple customer installs where offline bundles ballooned due to full apt repo mirrors and stale OCI images being kept indefinitely. This caused long transfer times during pre-seed and pushed some customers to request manual pruning support. ENG-4218 asked for a first-class solution to: (a) synthesize a minimal apt snapshot that contains only package metadata and binary diffs needed by target systems, and (b) lifecycle-manage the local OCI registries used to seed clusters during offline installs. This PR implements a pragmatic approach that is backwards compatible with the bundle loader in the private installer.

What changed (high level):
- New binary: tools/apt-snapshot/indexer: implements a delta-apt-index algorithm that computes required Packages.gz/Release fragments and a 'manifest-deb-list' which lists exact package files to include. The indexer supports suite matching (bionic/focal/jammy/bookworm), architecture filtering (amd64/arm64), and excludes source-only packages.
- New binary: tools/oci/pruner: lightweight controller that runs as a Kubernetes CronJob in the installer maintenance namespace. It connects to the seeded OCI registry, computes layer reachability using manifest references, and deletes unreferenced blobs older than TTL. Supports dry-run mode, concurrency limit, and registry GC hooks for Harbor/Registry v2 proxies.
- Helm chart updates: charts/private-installer/templates/maintenance-cron.yaml and charts/private-installer/values.yaml now include enable flags for apt-indexer sidecar and oci-pruner CronJob, config options for TTL (days), concurrency, and retention thresholds. Sidecar mode mounts bundle workspace and exposes /apt-overlay for kubelet prefetchers in the init phase.
- Terraform module: modules/airgap-storage/main.tf exposes retention_days and prune_schedule variables and wires them into the maintenance CronJob configmap. Added new IAM policy docs for storage lifecycle rules.
- Preflight and upgrade hooks: installer/preflight/apt-check now reads the generated manifest-deb-list to verify that all artifacts are present; the upgrade path includes a migration script to convert full-mirror bundles to a delta-snapshot bundle (tools/apt-snapshot/migrate_full_to_snapshot).
- Tests: integration test harness additions under test/airgap verify indexer output for jammy/amd64 and validate prune dry-run semantics against a mocked registry.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Omar Velasquez (reviewer): "Nice incremental approach here. Two requests: (1) can we ensure the indexer emits checksums and a reproducible timestamp so installs are deterministic? (2) make dry-run the default for the pruner CronJob until we validate across 3 installs."
- Maya Chen (author): "Added a reproducible output flag --fixed-timestamp and wire dryRun=true into Helm values by default. Updated tests to assert checksum presence."
- Priya Nair: "Terraform change looks good but we need an example for customers that want 'keep-7-days, min-size 10GB' semantics. Also please add a short note about register GC incompatibilities for certain registry proxies."
- Maya Chen: "Added example in examples/airgap-storage/README.md, and added a compatibility matrix for Harbor and nginx-registry-proxy."
- Liam O'Connor: "Small nit: chart templating uses `.Values.pruner` in two places; can we centralize a helper?"
- Maya Chen: "Refactored templates to use _helpers.tpl for pruner naming."

CI and test notes: First CI run showed a flaky integration test (indexer_integration_test) failing due to race in tempdir cleanup. I fixed the harness to use t.TempDir and retriggered CI. Final status: all checks passed. Workflow summary:
- unit: pass
- integration-airgap (mock registry): pass (after rerun)
- lint/helm: pass
- tfsec: pass
- build: pass

Safety and rollout:
- This is backwards compatible. The indexer output is consumed by installer preflight; if the generated manifest-deb-list is absent, the installer falls back to full-mirror mode. Pruner is opt-in via Helm and Terraform variables and defaults to dry-run. We will enable live prune only after a controlled rollout to a small set of pilot customers.

Migration path: Included a migration helper tools/apt-snapshot/migrate_full_to_snapshot.sh that analyzes a full mirror bundle and emits a delta snapshot plus an include list; docs explain the steps for customers to migrate.

Merge: Squash and merge. Merge PR 928472 into main.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-4302: add telemetry for pruner runs and blob deletion metrics (latency, reclaimed_bytes).
- ENG-4327: make delta-apt-index incremental so subsequent runs compute diffs between snapshots instead of re-scanning entire mirror.

If you want to test locally: see charts/private-installer/README.md for a quickstart that runs the indexer against a small apt archive and starts the pruner in dry-run against the local registry container.
